aboutParagraph: A glossary of Minecraft speedrunning terms, strategies, tools, and community language.

terms.name: Any%
terms.definition: A speedrun category with no required completion percentage; runners reach the category's defined endpoint as fast as possible. In Minecraft: Java Edition Any% Glitchless, the run finishes when the credits begin after the runner enters the exit End portal, not when the Ender Dragon dies. Leaderboards separate Random Seed, Set Seed, and version groups.

terms.name: Bastion
terms.definition: Bastion is the common MCSR name for a Bastion Remnant, a Nether structure added in Minecraft 1.16. In Java 1.16.1 RSG and Ranked, runners route bastions for gold blocks, piglins, and chests, then obtain Ender Pearls, obsidian, string, and Fire Resistance through bartering and loot. The four layouts require different routes.

terms.name: Bastion Route
terms.definition: A Bastion Route is a practiced path through one of the four Bastion Remnant layouts. A route coordinates gold collection, chest looting, piglin positioning, and bartering so the runner can obtain needed resources quickly and safely. Bridge, Housing, Stables, and Treasure bastions require different routes, especially in Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG and Ranked runs.

terms.name: Blaze
terms.definition: A Blaze is a hostile Nether mob and the source of Blaze Rods. In MCSR, runners usually fight Blazes at a Nether Fortress spawner because the rods are required to craft Eyes of Ender. MCSR Ranked standardizes Blaze Rod drops and spawner timing so both racers receive comparable RNG.

terms.name: Blaze Rods
terms.definition: Blaze Rods are items dropped by Blazes. Each rod crafts into two Blaze Powder, and one powder combines with one Ender Pearl to make an Eye of Ender. Speedrunners obtain rods in Nether Fortresses; piglins do not barter Blaze Rods.

terms.name: Blind
terms.definition: Blind travel is a Java 1.16 RSG strategy in which a runner moves through the Nether to a selected coordinate and builds an exit portal without first using an Eye of Ender to learn the stronghold's direction or distance. The goal is to emerge near a first-ring Stronghold, after which an eye can correct the route. It is distinct from educated and calculated travel.

media.title: Blind and educated travel tutorial
media.caption: BoomerPlayz introduces practical blind-travel coordinates before explaining how an eye throw can refine the route.

terms.name: Bridge Bastion
terms.definition: Bridge Bastion is one of the four Bastion Remnant layouts. It is distinguished by its large ruined bridge and a prominent gold-block structure often called the gold chalice. Speedrun routes use its exposed gold and layout-specific piglin positions, so it is routed differently from Housing, Stables, and Treasure bastions.

media.title: Bridge bastion route tutorial
media.caption: A route demonstration showing the bridge layout, gold collection, piglin setup, and exits used in Java 1.16.1 runs.

terms.name: Calculated Travel
terms.definition: Calculated Travel is a Nether-travel method that estimates both the direction and distance to a stronghold from precise Eye of Ender measurements, usually with a calculator. The runner converts the estimated Overworld target to Nether coordinates and builds a second portal nearby. It can produce a much closer exit than a blind or direction-only travel.

media.title: Calculated travel explained
media.caption: Four demonstrates how measured eye information and a calculator produce a stronghold target for a precise second portal.

terms.name: Classic
terms.definition: In MCSR Ranked, Classic means winning a match without entering a Bastion. In broader Java 1.16 RSG discussion, the word can also describe older or no-bastion routes, where runners may barter with ordinary piglins for pearls but still obtain Blaze Rods by killing Blazes. The intended context should always be stated.

terms.name: Divine Travel
terms.definition: Divine Travel is a Java Edition 1.16.1 technique that uses the position of a Nether fossil in a particular chunk to infer where a stronghold can be reached through another portal. It depends on world-generation correlations and is highly version-specific. It does not work in MCSR Ranked, where the Overworld and Nether seeds are generated independently.

media.title: Divine travel tutorial
media.caption: k4yfour explains the version-specific fossil and chunk relationship used to choose a divine-travel exit portal.

terms.name: Educated Travel
terms.definition: Educated Travel is a two-portal Nether-travel method that uses an Eye of Ender throw after the first exit to learn the stronghold's direction. The runner re-enters the Nether, moves along the corresponding direction, and builds a second exit portal nearer the stronghold ring. It improves direction over a blind travel without calculating a precise stronghold position.

media.title: Educated travel demonstration
media.caption: The second half of this tutorial shows how a post-blind eye direction guides a return through the Nether toward a closer exit.

terms.name: Elo
terms.definition: Elo is the rating used by MCSR Ranked to match players of similar skill and order its competitive ladder. Winning normally raises a player's Elo and losing lowers it, with the change influenced by the opponent's rating. The official styling is `Elo`, not the acronym `ELO`.

terms.name: Ender Pearl
terms.definition: An Ender Pearl is a throwable item that teleports the player to where it lands and is also an ingredient in an Eye of Ender. In Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG, runners commonly obtain pearls by bartering with piglins, usually at a bastion. Extra pearls can also save travel time or enable safer movement.

terms.name: Eye of Ender
terms.definition: An Eye of Ender is crafted from one Ender Pearl and one Blaze Powder. Thrown eyes travel toward the nearest Stronghold and may drop or break; runners measure their direction to navigate or triangulate. Eyes also fill the twelve End portal frames, although some frames can generate already filled.

terms.name: F3
terms.definition: F3 usually means the Java Edition debug screen and its related key combinations. It exposes information such as coordinates, facing direction, chunk position, and entity counts, which supports navigation, structure detection, and stronghold measurements. Available fields and permitted uses can depend on the game version and category rules.

terms.name: Filtered Seed
terms.definition: A Filtered Seed is a randomly generated seed accepted only when it meets predefined conditions. Filtering can reduce uncompetitive starts without giving runners a memorized Set Seed route. MCSR Ranked filters its Overworld and Nether seeds separately, so its seed generation differs from ordinary RSG.

terms.name: Housing Bastion
terms.definition: Housing Bastion is one of the four Bastion Remnant layouts. It contains two ramparts connected through a central housing section, with layout-specific gold, chests, and piglin positions. Runners identify it quickly because its safe and efficient route differs from Bridge, Stables, and Treasure bastions.

media.title: Housing bastion route tutorial
media.caption: A complete housing-units route demonstration covering recognition, gold collection, piglin positioning, and safe exits.

terms.name: Hypermodern
terms.definition: Hypermodern is a selective, reset-heavy route family developed for Java 1.16.1 RSG. It combines favorable coastal or mapless starts, rapid Nether entry, Bastion routing, fortress discovery, Nether travel, and an optimized End fight. It is not a universal label for every modern Minecraft version or for MCSR Ranked's filtered seeds.

terms.name: IGT
terms.definition: IGT means In-Game Time, a timing method that counts time according to the game's active run state rather than every second of wall-clock time. Minecraft Java Edition leaderboard rules exclude specified loading, pausing, and freeze periods from IGT, with approved timing tools or retiming used to determine the submitted time. Exact timing rules depend on the category.

terms.name: Leaderboard
terms.definition: A Leaderboard lists accepted run times for a category and its variables. Minecraft Java Edition runners submit evidence for moderator verification, and the resulting placement is meaningful only within that board's rules, version, difficulty, and seed-type filters.

terms.name: LiveSplit
terms.definition: LiveSplit is an open-source speedrun timer that records segment splits and compares attempts with saved runs. Minecraft runners can use it to display pace and personal-best comparisons, but the visible timer is not automatically the official leaderboard time; the category's timing rules still control.

terms.name: Mapless
terms.definition: Mapless is a Java Edition technique for locating buried treasure without a treasure map. The runner first uses a version-specific Pie Chart path and chunk-boundary behavior to identify the chunk containing the chest, then digs at chunk-relative X/Z coordinates `9, 9`. The `9, 9` position alone does not reveal which chunk contains treasure.

media.title: Mapless buried treasure tutorial
media.caption: MoleyG demonstrates the Pie Chart and chunk-position process used to identify and dig a buried treasure chest without a map.

terms.name: MCSR Ranked
terms.definition: MCSR Ranked is a Minecraft: Java Edition 1.16.1 Fabric mod and competitive format for live speedrun races. Standard matches put two players in separate worlds using the same filtered match seed and standardized RNG; the first player to defeat the dragon and enter the exit portal wins. Ranked matchmaking uses Elo and six ranks: Coal, Iron, Gold, Emerald, Diamond, and Netherite. The project also offers Casual, Private Rooms, and Weekly Race modes.

terms.name: Minecraft Speedrunning
terms.definition: Minecraft speedrunning is the practice of completing a defined Minecraft objective under a category's rules as quickly as possible. A prominent example is Java Edition Any% Glitchless Random Seed, where the runner starts an unknown world, reaches the End, defeats the Ender Dragon, and enters the exit portal. Other editions, categories, seeds, and version groups use different rules.

terms.name: Multi-Instance
terms.definition: Multi-Instance is an RSG setup that runs multiple separate Minecraft clients so worlds can generate in parallel and the runner can evaluate more starts. Official leaderboard rules place recording and installation requirements on this setup. SeedQueue offers a different way to queue generated worlds inside one game instance.

terms.name: Nether Fortress
terms.definition: A Nether Fortress is a Nether structure whose Blaze spawners provide the Blaze Rods required for Eyes of Ender. In Java 1.16.1 routes, runners often visit a Bastion first for pearls, obsidian, and Fire Resistance, then locate and navigate a fortress for rods. Fortress layout and spawner access strongly affect a run's pace.

media.title: Nether fortress navigation
media.caption: Lucas Chan explains fortress structure pieces and navigation cues that help runners locate a Blaze spawner efficiently.

terms.name: Nether Travel
terms.definition: Nether Travel uses the Nether's 1:8 horizontal coordinate scale to cover Overworld distance quickly. In Java Edition RSG, a runner can build another portal in the Nether so its Overworld exit is closer to a stronghold. Blind, Educated Travel, and Calculated Travel differ in how precisely the runner estimates that destination.

media.title: Nether coordinate scaling
media.caption: An original diagram showing why 100 blocks of horizontal Nether travel correspond to 800 Overworld blocks.
media.alt: Overworld and Nether lanes showing an eight-to-one horizontal coordinate scale

terms.name: Ninjabrain Bot
terms.definition: Ninjabrain Bot is an external stronghold calculator for Minecraft Java Edition speedrunning. It combines measured Eye of Ender throws, player-entered uncertainty, and stronghold-generation probabilities to estimate a location and confidence level. Runners use it for triangulation and Calculated Travel; its legality should always be checked against the current category rules.

terms.name: Obsidian
terms.definition: Obsidian is the block used to build Nether portal frames. In Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG, runners commonly obtain it from bastion chests and piglin bartering rather than mining it. Extra obsidian enables a second portal for Nether Travel and can also be useful during the End fight.

terms.name: One Cycle
terms.definition: A one cycle defeats the Ender Dragon during a single perch at the exit portal. In modern Java speedruns, runners normally time bed explosions against the dragon's head as it perches; respawn-anchor variants or backups also exist. The technique depends on the post-1.9 dragon fight and does not describe older pre-1.9 End fights.

media.title: One-cycle Ender Dragon tutorial
media.caption: Marcus Fireworks breaks down bed placement, timing, and damage during the dragon's perch at the exit portal.

terms.name: Pace
terms.definition: Pace describes how an attempt is progressing toward a time goal such as a personal best or world record. Runners infer pace from the current time, route state, resources, and splits. Being on a particular pace is a projection, not a guarantee of the final time.

terms.name: PB
terms.definition: PB means personal best: a runner's fastest valid completion in a particular category, ruleset, and timing method. A runner can therefore have separate PBs for RSG, Set Seed, different version groups, or different timing methods.

terms.name: Perch
terms.definition: A Perch is the Ender Dragon's landing sequence at the central exit portal. Runners prepare beds around the portal and wait for a favorable perch because it creates the main window for a One Cycle. Perch behavior is partly random and can be standardized by formats such as MCSR Ranked.

media.title: How the Ender Dragon perches
media.caption: T_Wagz explains the dragon's perch sequence and the cues runners watch while preparing a bed-based finish.

terms.name: Pie Chart
terms.definition: The Pie Chart is Java Edition's debug profiler graph, toggled with `F3+1` in current versions and historically with `Shift+F3`. Speedrunners navigate its numbered profiler sections and combine block-entity or spawner data with render-distance and chunk-boundary changes to locate structures. This use is often called pie-ray or piedar, and both profiler paths and exact procedures are version-specific.

terms.name: Piglin Bartering
terms.definition: Piglin Bartering is giving gold ingots to adult piglins in exchange for randomized items. In Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG, barters can provide Ender Pearls, obsidian, string, and fire resistance, making bastion routing central to many runs. Later 1.16 versions use a different barter table, and Blaze Rods never come from bartering.

terms.name: Random Seed
terms.definition: Random Seed is a speedrun seed type in which the seed input is left blank and the runner does not choose the world in advance. The official Java rules require a blank seed field. Random Seed describes seed knowledge; RSG additionally specifies a glitchless ruleset.

terms.name: Reset
terms.definition: A reset is abandoning the current attempt and starting another world. RSG runners reset when a seed no longer meets the requirements of their chosen route. Official Java rules allow specified reset mods and player-triggered reset macros, but macros generally cannot be triggered during gameplay.

terms.name: RNG Standardization
terms.definition: RNG Standardization is MCSR Ranked's system for making selected random events more consistent between races. It controls defined events such as barters, drops, Eye of Ender breaks, and parts of the dragon fight so a match depends less on extreme luck. It does not remove all randomness from a seed or route.

terms.name: RSG
terms.definition: RSG means Random Seed Glitchless, the ruleset behind many prominent Minecraft Any% runs. The runner starts an unknown seed and completes the category without techniques classified as glitches by the leaderboard rules. Edition and version groups still matter, so `1.16 RSG` is more specific than RSG alone.

terms.name: RTA
terms.definition: RTA means Real-Time Attack and measures elapsed real time from start to finish, normally including loads and pauses unless a category says otherwise. It contrasts with In-Game Time. Minecraft Java Edition leaderboard categories commonly use IGT, so runners should not assume an RTA display is the submitted time.

terms.name: Seed
terms.definition: A seed is the value Minecraft uses as an input when generating a world. Reusing a seed with the same relevant game version and settings can reproduce major terrain and structures, which makes chosen seeds suitable for Set Seed competition. Random Seed runs leave the seed field blank instead.

terms.name: SeedQueue
terms.definition: SeedQueue is a reset-management mod that generates multiple random worlds in the background and presents them for selection while using one Minecraft instance. It reduces waiting between RSG attempts and is an alternative to traditional multi-instancing. Leaderboard runners must follow the current rules for its version, configuration, recording, and queue limits.

terms.name: Set Seed
terms.definition: Set Seed is a speedrun seed type in which the runner enters and knows the seed before the attempt. This allows a planned route to be practiced and optimized. `SSG` commonly means Set Seed Glitchless in Minecraft Any%, while Set Seed by itself describes seed selection rather than every other category rule.

terms.name: Spawn
terms.definition: Spawn is the location where the player first enters a new world. In RSG, runners quickly evaluate nearby terrain, structures, food, iron, and Nether-entry options before deciding whether to continue or reset. Ranked starts are generated under its own filtering and standardization rules.

terms.name: Speedrun.com
terms.definition: Speedrun.com is the platform that hosts the main community-run Minecraft: Java Edition leaderboards. Its game pages publish category rules and accept run submissions that volunteer moderators verify. The site is not operated by Mojang, and runners should consult the current rules before recording or submitting a run.

terms.name: Split
terms.definition: A split is the cumulative time recorded when a runner reaches a chosen checkpoint; a segment is the time between two splits. MCSR runners might split on Nether entry, Nether exit, End entry, and the final exit-portal transition, but layouts are personal rather than an official fixed list. Timer tools compare current splits against a PB or another target.

terms.name: Stables Bastion
terms.definition: Stables Bastion is one of the four Bastion Remnant layouts. Its hoglin-stable sections, multiple ramparts, and distributed loot create routing and safety problems distinct from the other layouts. Speedrun routes account for its variable structure pieces, hoglins, gold access, and piglin collection.

media.title: Stables bastion route tutorial
media.caption: A layout-specific stables route showing how runners manage hoglins, distributed gold, piglins, and exits.

terms.name: Stronghold
terms.definition: A Stronghold is an underground Overworld structure containing an End portal room. Eyes of Ender point runners toward the nearest Stronghold, and the portal activates when all twelve frame slots contain eyes. Locating the correct chunk and navigating from the starter staircase to the portal room are separate MCSR skills.

media.title: Stronghold navigation tutorial
media.caption: k4yfour explains how structure generation and starter-staircase cues help runners find the portal room quickly.

terms.name: Treasure Bastion
terms.definition: Treasure Bastion is one of the four Bastion Remnant layouts. It has a large central treasure room with lava, gold blocks, and a magma cube spawner. That vertical, hazardous layout requires its own route for collecting gold and bartering without losing time or dying.

media.title: Treasure bastion route tutorial
media.caption: A practical route through the treasure room's vertical layout, lava hazards, gold blocks, and piglin setup.

terms.name: Triangulation
terms.definition: Triangulation estimates a stronghold location by comparing Eye of Ender directions from two or more measured positions. The intersection of those direction lines gives a target estimate. Tools such as stronghold calculators can account for measurement error, but accurate throws and inputs still matter.

media.title: Stronghold triangulation tutorial
media.caption: BoomerPlayz demonstrates how two measured Eye of Ender throws can estimate the point where their direction lines meet.

media.title: Two-throw triangulation diagram
media.caption: An original conceptual diagram showing two observed eye directions intersecting near an estimated stronghold position.
media.alt: Two green eye-direction lines from separate throws intersecting at a highlighted stronghold estimate

terms.name: WR
terms.definition: WR means world record: the fastest accepted valid time on a specified category and variables leaderboard at a given point in time. For Minecraft, edition, seed type, glitch rules, version group, and timing method can all distinguish records, so the live leaderboard is more reliable than a hard-coded holder or time.

terms.name: Zero Cycle
terms.definition: A zero cycle is an advanced End-fight technique that intercepts and kills the Ender Dragon during its initial flight, before a normal perch cycle. Established setups use a specific End spike, orientation, height, and timed bed or respawn-anchor explosions. Exact setups depend on the Minecraft version and on whether the run is vanilla RSG or MCSR Ranked.

media.title: Zero-cycle Ender Dragon tutorial
media.caption: T_Wagz demonstrates a precise zero-cycle setup and explains the positioning and explosion timing behind the technique.
